subject: Sensitive: Offboarding plan & records hold for case 1274
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-15T08:07:00Z
Subject: Sensitive: proposed involuntary separation — initial coordination (case 1274)

Team —

Following the PIP review and the last incident log, the people ops recommendation is to move forward with an involuntary separation for the employee tied to internal case 1274 (engineering IC). I am initiating coordination now so HR/legal/security are aligned on timing and deliverables.

High‑level asks:
- Confirm severance band we can offer (range and whether we can do a release + mutual NDA).
- Confirm payroll cutoff and final pay date (Monica).
- Security: confirm immediate account disable process and device retrieval (Evelyn).
- Legal: please review attached performance summary for risk assessment and any statutory requirements (looping counsel separately).

I attached a short performance summary and timeline notes. We are aiming for a discrete in‑person conversation on Wednesday 11/19 AM PT, with termination effective immediately following the meeting (if HR/legal sign off).

This is sensitive — please do not copy wider distribution or add this to Slack.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Engineering (Platform)
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
[attachment: performance_summary_1274.pdf]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-15T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Sensitive: proposed involuntary separation — initial coordination (case 1274)

Jonas —

Thanks for the heads up and for the summary. I reviewed the doc and the prior PIP notes. My preliminary read: risk is moderate but manageable with a standard mutual release and a non‑disparagement clause. Recommend 8 weeks base pay + continuation of benefits through the end of the month. If you want to increase to 12 weeks we'll need exec approval and to document business rationale.

Monica, can you confirm payroll timing and whether we can front‑pay severance to speed closure? Also confirm whether final paycheck will include accrued PTO and how we handle equity vesting (notification to Compensation team).

Assuming legal signs off, we should aim for the 11/19 meeting as proposed. I will join if available.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-15T14:13:00Z
Subject: Re: Sensitive: proposed involuntary separation — initial coordination (case 1274)

Thanks — tracking here. A few notes from HR ops: 
- Payroll: we can do 8 weeks severance as a lump sum to be issued on the final pay date (can also do a front‑pay option but requires finance signoff — I'll request).
- PTO: accrued PTO will be paid out per policy; will include in the final calculation.
- Benefits: we can continue health benefits for the severance period if we process COBRA enrollment notices promptly (will send package).
- Equity: Compensation needs the employee's grant IDs to confirm accelerated vesting eligibility (I will open a case).

Checklist items for the termination meeting:
1) Final written severance offer (draft attached — Severance_Template_v1.docx).
2) Signed mutual release + DocuSign workflow.
3) Badge + laptop return logistics (we can collect same day at campus security desk).
4) Access revocation schedule (Evelyn to confirm).
5) Workday termination entry and final pay code.

Please let me know if we should nudge finance for front‑pay. Also, advise if you want to offer outplacement.

Monica

--
Monica Patel
Senior HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
[attachment: Severance_Template_v1.docx]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-16T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Sensitive: proposed involuntary separation — initial coordination (case 1274)

Appreciate the checklist, Monica. A couple of operational details / requests: 
- Please keep the process minimal and in person; no Slack or mass emails.
- For device retrieval: can security do a same‑day asset pickup (we'll bring the payload to the desk)? If not, we need a couriers/process note.
- Access: we need an ordered disable plan — disable interactive logins first, then API keys, then service account credentials, and finally re‑key any shared accounts the engineer had access to (particularly the model‑serving admin role). Evelyn, can you outline the timed steps and whether we can do an automatic snapshot of the employee's cloud activity (logs) before disabling for audit?

Also — please do not include compensation numbers in general notes; keep them to the severance doc.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-17T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Sensitive: proposed involuntary separation — initial coordination (case 1274)

Jonas / Monica —

Security plan below (high‑level) — attaching playbook for reference (access_revocation_playbook.pdf). We can execute this with a T+5 / T+15 / T+60 minute cadence relative to the termination meeting.

T0 (termination meeting ends):
- Disable interactive logins (VPN, Okta) — immediate (T+5).
- Revoke SSH and console keys provisioned to the user (T+5).
- Rotate any service account keys the user had access to (T+15) — will need confirmation of list; I will request owners to rotate.
- Revoke cloud provider console sessions and revoke STS tokens (T+15).
- Remove from all Slack/public channels and reset SSO session tokens (automated via Okta sync) (T+5).
- Snapshot relevant audit logs (compute, object storage, model serving logs) and export to secure archive — do not purge; this goes to Legal hold (we will preserve for 180 days).
- Disable email access and set auto‑reply as directed by HR (T+5).

Device return: campus security can accept laptop and charger same day and tag assets 'returned under HR case 1274'. If employee is remote, we can trigger prepaid courier pickup (Monica to authorize).

Permission/keys note: we will need a short inventory of service accounts and shared keys the employee touched — Jonas, can your team produce the list by EOD tomorrow? That will speed rotations.

Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
[attachment: access_revocation_playbook.pdf]

From: Patricia Naylor <pnaylor@counselpartners.com>

Date: 2025-11-18T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Sensitive: proposed involuntary separation — initial coordination (case 1274)

Laura / Monica / Jonas —

I reviewed the template and the performance summary. Attached is a revised severance agreement (Severance_Agreement_v2.pdf) that includes:
- 8 weeks base pay (lump sum) as proposed; option noted for 12 weeks with exec sign‑off.
- Mutual release language and a narrow non‑disparagement clause (we softened employer obligations for gradations).
- A brief carve‑out preserving employee's right to file government claims (standard).
- DocuSign ready — I recommend we include a 7‑day review period for the employee to consider the agreement and ensure valid waiver language.

With respect to evidence preservation: we will accept the log snapshot as long as chain‑of‑custody metadata is preserved (who exported, when, and where it is stored). Do not alter or delete the exported files.

If you approve the attached language, I can prepare final DocuSign envelopes and handle the e‑sign flow.

Patricia Naylor
Counsel Partners LLP
pnaylor@counselpartners.com
[attachment: Severance_Agreement_v2.pdf]
